title: Quarter-Wave Initialized 4-Layer AR-Cr Stack
scientific_hypothesis: Constraining thickness initialization bounds to ±15% of quarter-wave optical thickness (QWOT) at 550 nm will reduce optimizer search space waste and improve convergence toward higher target scores compared to the unconstrained 350-499 nm range observed in route_04.
design_principle: Admittance locus method with quarter-wave initialization: each dielectric layer thickness initialized near λ/4n at the center of the visible absorption band (550 nm) to establish constructive/destructive interference conditions that minimize visible reflectance while the Cr layer provides IR reflectance.
proposed_topology: Air | SiO2 (layer 1) | Cr (layer 2) | HfO2 (layer 3) | SiO2 (layer 4) | Al substrate. Total finite layers: 4.
manufacturing_considerations: Cr thickness should remain thin (<100 nm) for partial transparency in visible
dielectric layers near QWOT for manufacturability
theory_basis: Quarter-wave optical thickness principle: QWOT = λ_center / (4 × n), where λ_center = 550 nm for visible band
Admittance locus tracking for layer-by-layer reflectance prediction
expected_advantages: Reduced optimizer iteration count due to tighter initialization bounds
Layer 4 thickness constrained to ~94 nm ±15% instead of 350-499 nm wasted range
known_risks: QWOT initialization may be too restrictive if optimal solution lies outside ±15% bounds
4-layer topology may have limited design freedom compared to previous iteration
execution_request_english: Optimize a 4-layer spectrally selective absorber stack on aluminum substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: SiO2 | Cr | HfO2 | SiO2 | Al. Wavelength bands: 400-700 nm (maximize absorptance, minimize reflectance), 700-2000 nm (maximize reflectance). Initialize layer thicknesses at quarter-wave optical thickness centered on 550 nm with ±15% bounds: SiO2 layer 1 at 94.2 nm ±15%, Cr layer 2 at 30 nm ±50% (absorbing layer), HfO2 layer 3 at 68.75 nm ±15%, SiO2 layer 4 at 94.2 nm ±15%. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer. Normal incidence, unpolarized illumination. Total layer count: 4 finite layers. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 400-700 nm, 700-2000 nm. soft objectives: high absorptance in 400-700 nm; low reflectance in 400-700 nm; high reflectance in 700-2000 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflectance in 400-700 nm; high absorptance in 700-2000 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count not exceeding 20.
revision_reason: Applied feedback directive to constrain initialization bounds for layers 2-4 to ±15% of QWOT at 550 nm. Previous route_04 showed layer 4 fluctuating between 350-499 nm representing wasted phase space. This refinement funnels optimizer into high-transmission neighborhood with tighter bounds.
